title: Dasaratha passes away
introduction: At the dawn of the next day, panergysts and servants arrived at the palace to serve the king. Some women, who were empowered to go near the bed, detected the king's death and started crying loudly. Kausalya and Sumitra suddenly woke up from their slumber and came to know of the king's death. All the wives of Dasaratha wept miserably. The gynaecium was filled with men and women who felt bewildered with fear and restlessness; when the king met with his appointed end.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चषष्टितमः सर्गः
Thus completes 65th Chapter of Ayodhya Kanda of the glorious Ramayana of Valmiki, the work of a sage and the oldest epic.

verses.devanagari:
अथ रात्र्याम् व्यतीतायाम् प्रातर् एव अपरे अहनि |
वन्दिनः पर्युपातिष्ठंस् तत् पार्थिव निवेशनम्
सूताः परमसंस्काराः मङ्गळाश्चोओत्तमश्रुताः |
गायकाः स्तुतिशीलाश्च निगदन्तः पृथक् पृथक्
verses.iast:
atha rātryām vyatītāyām prātar eva apare ahani |
vandinaḥ paryupātiṣṭhaṃs tat pārthiva niveśanam
sūtāḥ paramasaṃskārāḥ maṇ^gaLāścoottamaśrutāḥ |
gāyakāḥ stutiśīlāśca nigadantaḥ pṛthak pṛthak
verses.translation: While the night passed away, there arrived at the residence of the emperor, at the dawn of the next day, highly cultured and excellently learned bards who were pronouncers of benedictions and whose custom was to eulogize the king, as well as singers and panegyrists uttering recitations in different styles.

glosses.meaning: and whose custom was to eulogize the king

verses.devanagari:
राजानम् स्तुताम् तेषामुदात्ताभिहिताशिषाम् |
प्रासादाभोगविस्तीर्णः स्तुतिशब्दो ह्यवर्तत
verses.iast:
rājānam stutām teṣāmudāttābhihitāśiṣām |
prāsādābhogavistīrṇaḥ stutiśabdo hyavartata
verses.translation: Their sounds of praises, uttering benedictions in a loud voice and pronouncing accolades of the king, pervaded in full the interior area of the palace.

glosses.meaning: uttering benedictions in a loud voice

verses.devanagari:
ततस्तु स्तुवताम् तेषाम् सूतानाम् पाणिवादकाः |
अवदानान्युदाहृत्य पाणिवादा नवादयन्
verses.iast:
tatastu stuvatām teṣām sūtānām pāṇivādakāḥ |
avadānānyudāhṛtya pāṇivādā navādayan
verses.translation: While those bards are uttering praises, others who make a bang of claps, patted the claps, eulogizing the previous glorious acts of Dasaratha.

glosses.meaning: some others who make noises of claps

verses.devanagari:
तेन शब्देन विहगाः प्रतिबुद्धा विसस्वनुः |
शाखास्थाः पञ्जरस्थाश्च ये राजकुलगोचराः
verses.iast:
tena śabdena vihagāḥ pratibuddhā visasvanuḥ |
śākhāsthāḥ paJṇjarasthāśca ye rājakulagocarāḥ
verses.translation: The birds dwelling in royal palaces perched on the branches of trees and others in cages were awakened by that sound and began to twitter.

verses.devanagari:
व्याहृताः पुण्य्शब्दाश्च वीणानाम् चापि निस्स्वनाः |
आशीर्गेयम् च गाथानाम् पूरयामास वेश्म तत
verses.iast:
vyāhṛtāḥ puṇyśabdāśca vīṇānām cāpi nissvanāḥ |
āśīrgeyam ca gāthānām pūrayāmāsa veśma tata
verses.translation: The auspicious words uttered by bards parrots etc and the notes of Vina as well as blissful songs of the metric verses filled that palace.

verses.devanagari:
ततः शुचि समाचाराः पर्युपस्थान कोविदः |
स्त्री वर्ष वर भूयिष्ठाउपतस्थुर् यथा पुरम्
verses.iast:
tataḥ śuci samācārāḥ paryupasthāna kovidaḥ |
strī varṣa vara bhūyiṣṭhāupatasthur yathā puram
verses.translation: Then, as before, persons who maintain pure practices and those who were skilled in the services to the king, most of whom were women and eunuchs, arrived there to serve the king.

glosses.meaning: and those who were skilled in the services to the king
most of whom were women and eunuchs

verses.devanagari:
हरि चन्दन सम्पृक्तम् उदकम् कान्चनैः घटैः |
आनिन्युः स्नान शिक्षा आज्ञा यथा कालम् यथा विधि
verses.iast:
hari candana sampṛktam udakam kāncanaiḥ ghaṭaiḥ |
āninyuḥ snāna śikṣā āGYā yathā kālam yathā vidhi
verses.translation: Those who took care of royal ablutions brought water sprinkled with yellow sandal in golden pitchers in accordance with appropriate time and the set procedures.

glosses.meaning: those who took care of royal ablutions
in accordance with the appropriate time
and according to the set procedures.

verses.devanagari:
मन्गल आलम्भनीयानि प्राशनीयान् उपस्करान् |
उपनिन्युस् तथा अपि अन्याः कुमारी बहुलाः स्त्रियः
verses.iast:
mangala ālambhanīyāni prāśanīyān upaskarān |
upaninyus tathā api anyāḥ kumārī bahulāḥ striyaḥ
verses.translation: In that manner, women too most of whom were virgins brought all that were pleasing to the touch, eatables, decorative clothing and ornaments.

glosses.meaning: all that were pleasing to touch praashaniiyaan = eatables

verses.devanagari:
सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्नम् सर्वम् विधिवदर्चितम् |
सर्वम् सुगुणलक्स्मीवत्तद्भभूवाभिहारिकम्
verses.iast:
sarvalakśaṇasampannam sarvam vidhivadarcitam |
sarvam suguṇalaksmīvattadbhabhūvābhihārikam
verses.translation: All that was brought near him was endowed with all auspicious characteristics offered with reverence as per prescribed scriptures. All that was extremely graceful.

verses.devanagari:
ततः सूर्योदयम् यावत्सर्वम् परिसमुत्सुकम् |
तस्थावनुपसम्प्राप्तम् किम् स्विदित्युपश्
verses.iast:
tataḥ sūryodayam yāvatsarvam parisamutsukam |
tasthāvanupasamprāptam kim svidityupaś
verses.translation: All that retinue, greatly excited as they were, without coming near to the king and with a suspicion as to what was it, stayed thus till sunrise.

glosses.meaning: without coming near to the king

verses.devanagari:
अथ याः कोसल इन्द्रस्य शयनम् प्रत्यनन्तराः |
ताः स्त्रियः तु समागम्य भर्तारम् प्रत्यबोधयन्
verses.iast:
atha yāḥ kosala indrasya śayanam pratyanantarāḥ |
tāḥ striyaḥ tu samāgamya bhartāram pratyabodhayan
verses.translation: The women who were empowered to go near the bed of Dasaratha went in proximity to him and woke him up.

verses.devanagari:
तथाप्युचितवृत्तास्ता विनयेन नयेन च |
न ह्यस्य शयनम् स्पृष्ट्वा किम् चिदप्युपलेभिरे
verses.iast:
tathāpyucitavṛttāstā vinayena nayena ca |
na hyasya śayanam spṛṣṭvā kim cidapyupalebhire
verses.translation: Even so, those modest and prudent women with proper conduct, touched Dasaratha's bed and could not detect any sign of life whatsoever in him.

verses.devanagari:
ताः स्त्रीयः स्वप्नशीलज्ञास्चेष्टासंचलनादिषु |
ता वेपथु परीताः च राज्ञः प्राणेषु शन्किताः
प्रतिस्रोतः तृण अग्राणाम् सदृशम् संचकम्पिरे |
verses.iast:
tāḥ strīyaḥ svapnaśīlajJṇāsceṣṭāsaṃcalanādiṣu |
tā vepathu parītāḥ ca rāGYaḥ prāṇeṣu śankitāḥ
pratisrotaḥ tṛṇa agrāṇām sadṛśam saṃcakampire |
verses.translation: Those women knew the condition of a body in sleep, by its gestures, movements and others. As such, they were possessed of tremor apprehensive as they were about the king's life and they resembled like tips of reeds standing against a stream.

glosses.meaning: knew the condition of a body in sleep
like tips of reeds standing against a stream.

verses.devanagari:
अथ सम्वेपमनानाम् स्त्रीणाम् दृष्ट्वा च पार्थिवम्
यत् तत् आशन्कितम् पापम् तस्य जज्ञे विनिश्चयः |
verses.iast:
atha samvepamanānām strīṇām dṛṣṭvā ca pārthivam
yat tat āśankitam pāpam tasya jaGYe viniścayaḥ |
verses.translation: Now, seeing the king, certainty arose in the minds of those doubting women about the calamity (of death) that was apprehended.

verses.devanagari:
कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च पुत्रशोकपराजिते
प्रसुप्ते न प्रबुध्येते यथा कालसमन्विते |
verses.iast:
kausalyā ca sumitrā ca putraśokaparājite
prasupte na prabudhyete yathā kālasamanvite |
verses.translation: Overpowered by grief for their sons, the slumbering Kausalya and Sumitra did not wake up, as though they were completely overtaken by death.

glosses.meaning: overpowered by grief for their sons
as if they were completely possessed of death.

verses.devanagari:
निष्प्रभा च विवर्णा च सन्ना शोकेन सन्नता
न व्यराजत कौसल्या तारेव तिमिरावृता |
verses.iast:
niṣprabhā ca vivarṇā ca sannā śokena sannatā
na vyarājata kausalyā tāreva timirāvṛtā |
verses.translation: Kausalya bereft of luster, pale faced, emaciated with grief and dispirited, did not shine brightly (as before) like a star hidden away in darkness.

verses.devanagari:
कौसल्यानन्तरम् राज्ञः सुमित्रा तदन्तनरम्
न स्म विभ्राजते देवी शोकाश्रुलुलितानना |
verses.iast:
kausalyānantaram rājJṇaḥ sumitrā tadantanaram
na sma vibhrājate devī śokāśrululitānanā |
verses.translation: The queen Kausalya, immediately close to the king and with Sumitra on her side, was not shining as before with her face ruffled by tears of grief.

glosses.meaning: with her face ruffled by tears of grief.

verses.devanagari:
ते च दृष्ट्वा तथा सुप्ते शुभे देव्यौ च तम् नृपम्
सुप्तमे वोद्गतप्राणमन्तः पुरमन्यत |
verses.iast:
te ca dṛṣṭvā tathā supte śubhe devyau ca tam nṛpam
suptame vodgataprāṇamantaḥ puramanyata |
verses.translation: The persons in the gynaecium, having seen those distinguished queens in slumber and also the king in that manner, thought that the king had lost his life while just sleeping.

glosses.meaning: that the king had lost his life

verses.devanagari:
ततः प्रचुक्रुशुर् दीनाः सस्वरम् ता वर अन्गनाः
करेणवैव अरण्ये स्थान प्रच्युत यूथपाः |
verses.iast:
tataḥ pracukruśur dīnāḥ sasvaram tā vara anganāḥ
kareṇavaiva araṇye sthāna pracyuta yūthapāḥ |
verses.translation: Then, those beautiful women miserably cried loudly with their voice, like female elephants crying when their group leader an elephant was removed from their place in the forest.

verses.devanagari:
तासाम् आक्रन्द शब्देन सहसा उद्गत चेतने
कौसल्या च सुमित्राच त्यक्त निद्रे बभूवतुः |
verses.iast:
tāsām ākranda śabdena sahasā udgata cetane
kausalyā ca sumitrāca tyakta nidre babhūvatuḥ |
verses.translation: Kausalya and Sumitra suddenly obtained consciousness by the sound of their cries and woke up from sleep.

verses.devanagari:
कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च दृष्ट्वा स्पृष्ट्वा च पार्थिवम्
हा नाथ इति परिक्रुश्य पेततुर् धरणी तले |
verses.iast:
kausalyā ca sumitrā ca dṛṣṭvā spṛṣṭvā ca pārthivam
hā nātha iti parikruśya petatur dharaṇī tale |
verses.translation: Kausalya and Sumitra, on seeing and touching king Dasaratha, cried �O, Lord!' and fell on the ground.

verses.devanagari:
सा कोसल इन्द्र दुहिता वेष्टमाना मही तले
न बभ्राज रजो ध्वस्ता तारा इव गगन च्युता |
verses.iast:
sā kosala indra duhitā veṣṭamānā mahī tale
na babhrāja rajo dhvastā tārā iva gagana cyutā |
verses.translation: Rolling on the floor and covered by dust, Kausalya the daughter of Kosala king was not shining as before and resembled a star falling down from the sky.

verses.devanagari:
नृपे शान्तगुणे जाते कौसल्याम् पतिताम् भुवि
आपश्यंस्ताः स्त्रियः सर्वा हताम् नागवधूमिव |
verses.iast:
nṛpe śāntaguṇe jāte kausalyām patitām bhuvi
āpaśyaṃstāḥ striyaḥ sarvā hatām nāgavadhūmiva |
verses.translation: While the king was deceased, all the women saw Kausalya who fell on the floor appearing as a female elephant, which was killed and felled on the ground.

glosses.meaning: which was killed (and felled on ground).

verses.devanagari:
ततः सर्वा नरेन्द्रस्य कैकेयीप्रमुखाः स्त्रियः
रुदन्त्यः शोकसन्तप्ता निपेतुर्गतचेतनाः |
verses.iast:
tataḥ sarvā narendrasya kaikeyīpramukhāḥ striyaḥ
rudantyaḥ śokasantaptā nipeturgatacetanāḥ |
verses.translation: Kaikeyi and all other wives of king Dasaratha were weeping afflicted by grief and fell unconscious.

verses.devanagari:
ताभिः स बलवान्नादः क्रोशन्तीभिरनुद्रुतः
येन स्फीतीकृतो भूयस्तद्गृहम् समनादयत् |
verses.iast:
tābhiḥ sa balavānnādaḥ krośantībhiranudrutaḥ
yena sphītīkṛto bhūyastadgṛham samanādayat |
verses.translation: That great noise was supplemented by those wailing women, bloated by which, it rendered the house all the more noisy.

verses.devanagari:
तत् समुत्त्रस्त सम्भ्रान्तम् पर्युत्सुक जन आकुलम्
सर्वतः तुमुल आक्रन्दम् परिताप आर्त बान्धवम् |
सद्यो निपतित आनन्दम् दीन विक्लव दर्शनम्
बभूव नर देवस्य सद्म दिष्ट अन्तम् ईयुषः |
verses.iast:
tat samuttrasta sambhrāntam paryutsuka jana ākulam
sarvataḥ tumula ākrandam paritāpa ārta bāndhavam |
sadyo nipatita ānandam dīna viklava darśanam
babhūva nara devasya sadma diṣṭa antam īyuṣaḥ |
verses.translation: That gynaecium of the king who met his appointed end was filled with people who felt bewildered with fear and restlessness, with tumultuous wail all around, and crowded with relatives disturbed by sorrow, with happiness withered away in it suddenly and became a sight of misery and despondency.

glosses.meaning: was filled with people bewildered with fear and restlessness
a sight of misery and despondency.

verses.devanagari:
अतीतम् आज्ञाय तु पार्थिव ऋषभम् |
यशस्विनम् सम्परिवार्य पत्नयः |
भृशम् रुदन्त्यः करुणम् सुदुह्खिताः |
प्रगृह्य बाहू व्यलपन्न् अनाथवत् || २-६५-२९.
verses.iast:
atītam āGYāya tu pārthiva ṛṣabham |
yaśasvinam samparivārya patnayaḥ |
bhṛśam rudantyaḥ karuṇam suduhkhitāḥ |
pragṛhya bāhū vyalapann anāthavat || 2-65-29.
verses.translation: Knowing that the glorious king of excellence had passed away, the king's wives surrounded him with great sorrow; pitiably wailing profusely and lamented, grasping their hands one another, like orphans.
